# Results — Study 231 (Sloan Accruals) on the real EDGAR panel

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Signal: Sloan (1996) accruals
ratio (Net Income - Operating Cash Flow) / Average Total Assets from annual 10-K filings
via the shared EDGAR cache. Returns from `_edgar_yrret.parquet` (Yahoo Finance).
As-of **2026-06-16**.*

**Definition**:
- Accruals = Net Income - Operating Cash Flow
- Avg Assets = (Total Assets_t + Total Assets_{t-1}) / 2
- Accruals ratio = Accruals / Avg Assets

**Reporting lag**: fundamentals from fiscal year y → returns in calendar year y+1.
**Universe**: current S&P 500 members with all three concepts present (~300+ tickers/year).
**Window**: 17 years of signal (2009–2025), forecasting returns 2010–2026.

**SURVIVORSHIP-BIAS WARNING**: the EDGAR panel covers only current S&P 500 members
projected backwards. Every firm in the panel survived to 2026. All results are upper
bounds on a live strategy — the true live effect is weaker, possibly nonexistent.

## Verdict

The hedge nominally passes the |t|≥2 bar (HAC t = +2.73 on the hedge; t = +3.57 on the
low-accruals excess). However, these numbers are **inflated by survivorship bias**: the
panel covers only firms that remained in the S&P 500 to 2026. High-accrual firms that
over-stated earnings, hit earnings disappointments, and were expelled from the index are
absent — precisely the firms that would have hurt the high-accruals portfolio most.

More importantly: virtually all the hedge comes from the long leg. The high-accruals (Q5)
quintile earns essentially market return (−0.1%/yr excess, t = −0.04), not the dramatic
underperformance predicted by Sloan (1996). The low-accruals (Q1) excess (+5.7%/yr) may
reflect a quality/profitability tilt rather than pure accruals mispricing: cash-heavy
firms on the S&P 500 survivor panel tend to be high-quality compounders that naturally
outperform in a bull-market decade.

On a properly point-in-time universe (Compustat with historical S&P 500 constituents),
the Sloan anomaly has substantially decayed in the post-2000 era as arbitrageurs closed
it (Green, Hand & Soliman 2011; Richardson et al. 2010).

- **Signal — WEAK** (nominal HAC t = +2.73 on the hedge; but survivorship-biased upper
  bound, and the short-side barely contributes; literature shows the effect has decayed
  on large caps in the post-2000 sample).
- **Tradability — FRAGILE** (annual rebalancing is operationally cheap on S&P 500 names;
  but the alpha estimate is uncertain and the academic literature shows significant decay;
  on this biased panel, Investable is not warranted).
